phase_5_stateless_menu.notes: Session 2 (2026-08-30) — PLAN TABLE (written before code, per contract). Baseline verified on fresh clone: npm ci then npm test = 145/145 (phase-4 checkpoint accurate; the 6 initial failures were only missing node_modules). STATE SURFACE AUDIT — everything getState/putState/clearFlow currently carries: (A) state.flow + state.pending: the 12 input flows below. (B) state.activeViewId: the single self-editing view id (views.js renderInteractiveView/renderFreshView + the bug-01 reset in handleMessage). (C) state.currentTask: write-only leftover (set in startJob/startRelayJob after ensureTaskLabel, NEVER read anywhere) — dead, deleted outright. ENCODING DECISIONS: - Menu edits become message_id-implicit: every button-driven render edits callback.message.message_id; every user-message-driven render sends fresh (bug-01 behavior kept). activeViewId persistence deleted; views.js renderInteractiveView(messageId=null => fresh send, no getState/putState). - freeTextReply(env, chatId, text, options?) in telegram.js: sendMessage with reply_markup {force_reply:true, selective:true} (plus inline keyboard only when a Cancel/choice row is needed — Telegram allows both markups together; the inline rows go on the SAME message object). Returns the sent Message. - parseFlowReply(message) in new pure module src/flow.js: reads message.reply_to_message; returns {opcode,args,messageId} iff reply_to_message.from.is_bot && text parses marker '[cf] cf:[:arg…]' (single-line marker comment at the bottom of every prompt; documented in ARCHITECTURE.md). Matching is by OPCODE STRING, not message_id (message_id is only reported for callers that need to edit the prompt, e.g. clone progress) — matches the contract ('keyed off message.reply_to_message'). - Pending flow context is re-derived per reply: credentials come from KV getCredentials (allowed); jobId for upload_plan re-resolved via getJobIdForLabel(pending label arg). NO chat-state record is ever written for navigation. FLOW-BY-FLOW MAPPING (12 flows): 1. wizard (multi-step: source/focus text + duration/music buttons + confirm): - Text steps (source incl. .torrent/video documents, focus): prompt carries invisible marker 'cf:wzsrc' / 'cf:wzfoc' + force_reply; wizard record encoded in marker args. - Wizard state travels as opaque token arg on every wz:* callback_data and as marker args: legacy base64url(JSON wizard) prefixed '1' (v1). ~92 bytes for a fresh wizard => under the 64-byte CALLBACK cap it only rides as marker text (no cap on message text); for callbacks the token is NOT round-tripped — instead every wizard BUTTON message is itself a marker-bearing prompt? NO — simpler split: button-only steps (length/music/confirm) encode wizard fields FLATTENED in callback_data: 'wz:dur::' would exceed 64B. DECISION: button steps carry the full wizard inline: jobId(manual-<13digits>) + step + series(1bit) + duration + music-code fit; source/focus text DO NOT fit => source/focus completion is communicated via the user's force_reply REPLY whose reply_to_message chain anchors the wizard, and subsequent button steps re-encode from (a) flattened fields in the current message's marker + (b) the just-answered text. The full wizard object therefore lives ONLY in the latest prompt message's marker comment as base64url JSON (message text, no size cap); every wizard render embeds 'cf:wzs:' (step prompts) and button callbacks read it back from callback.message.text via parseWizardMarker(). callback_data stays tiny ('wz:dur:60' etc., unchanged). This is exactly 'encode the current step directly into each inline keyboard's message' — the keyboard's message carries the state. - wz:cancel / wz:back mutate the marker-carried wizard and re-render (edit). Expiry case = message has no parseable marker (e.g. very old message) => 'wizard expired, /new' (same UX as today). 2. upload_plan (label arg): prompt marker 'cf:upl:

human_review_items: Pre-existing deploy-blocker found on origin/main before migration work: tickCloneJob (bot/src/index.js) used `const job` + reassignment, so no Bot A build/deploy could succeed. Fixed to `let` as a prerequisite of phase 0's deploy gate. This bug predates the migration and affected ALL prior deploy attempts, not just D1 work.

phase_5 documented UX assumption (statelessness forces it): multi-bubble production.json pastes must reply to the bot's ⏳ receiving-indicator message (one tap in every client) instead of being bare consecutive sends — there is no stored flow left to attribute bare fragments to. Single-message pastes and .json files are unchanged (reply to the upload prompt).
phase_5 documented assumption: state.currentTask was write-only (set after task creation, never read anywhere) — deleted outright rather than re-homed.
